---
title: "check-precedence-parens.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags math leaving the precedence
of a logical connective implicit.
The lab's rule is that math we write uses parentheses
to make operator precedence explicit (Ezra, 2026-11-19),
so a union is written `\set{x : (x \in A) \lor (x \in B)}`
and not `\set{x : x \in A \lor x \in B}`.

The check reads `$...$` and `$$...$$` math
on lines a pull request adds,
in `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, and `.md` files,
and has two rules:

- **A relation beside a connective.**
  An operand of `\land`, `\lor`, `\wedge`, `\vee`, `\implies`, `\iff`,
  `\Rightarrow`, `\Leftrightarrow`, a long arrow, or a Unicode form of one
  holds an unparenthesized relation,
  such as `=`, `<`, `\le`, `\in`, `\notin`, `\subseteq`, `\equiv`, or `\mid`.
- **Two kinds of connective together.**
  Two different connectives sit at one level, as in `P \land Q \lor R`,
  or an implication or biconditional repeats, as in
  `P \Rightarrow Q \Rightarrow R`, which is not associative.
  A repeated `\land` or `\lor` passes.

Each finding reports the file, the line,
and the operand or the connectives it found.

## Operands and groups

An operand ends at a connective and at a separator:
`,`, `;`, `:`, `\colon`, `&`, `\\`, `\quad`, `\qquad`,
`\text{...}` and the other text commands,
a quantifier (`\forall`, `\exists`),
and a definition sign (`\eqdef`, `\coloneqq`, `:=`).
So the `x` before a set builder's colon is not an operand,
and a quantifier's domain (`\forall x \in A, P(x)`) ends at its comma.

A group is checked on its own:
parentheses, brackets, braces, `\{...\}`, angle brackets,
and a macro argument such as the one `\paren{...}` or `\set{...}` takes.
The relation inside `(x \in A)` belongs to that group,
not to the connective outside it.
Sizing commands (`\left`, `\right`, `\bigl`, ...) are ignored.

The check does not flag:

- the single arrows `\to`, `\rightarrow`, and `\leftrightarrow`,
  which the notes use for functions, limits, and paths
  far more than for implication;
- a connective that opens a clause,
  such as the `\iff` of an aligned derivation row (`&\iff x \in S`),
  which joins the row to the one before it;
- a code fence or code span, an HTML comment, or YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following, `<!-- check-precedence-parens: allow -->`,
  for example an exercise that shows an ungrouped form on purpose.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing pages never block,
and a page converts when someone edits it.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose,
for example to count the implicit precedences a repository still carries.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

## Limitations

- Each line is read on its own,
  so a group or operand split across lines is checked in pieces.
- A connective written in words (`\text{ or }`) is a separator,
  not a connective.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.Rmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `true`  | Fail the workflow when an implicit precedence is found. Set `false` to warn only. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-precedence-parens.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags math on lines a PR adds that leaves the precedence
# of a logical connective implicit, such as `x \in A \lor x \in B` (write
# `(x \in A) \lor (x \in B)`) or `P \land Q \lor R`.
# Blocks by default; existing pages never block, since only added lines count.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check that math parenthesizes around logical connectives

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-precedence-parens.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'mds/**,notes/**'         # skip submodules and known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                             # warn instead of block (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-precedence-parens.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-precedence-parens.yml)
for the full caller stub.
